C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.description: For any estimator passing C1, K3 >= 0.5 bits with p <= 0.001 on stochastic SPA
C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.note: C3 fails because the stochastic SPA's 50/50 mixing produces very weak CMI signals. KSG CMI is 0.000560 bits (26x below threshold). LR is 0.103695 bits (4.8x below threshold) and identical to the deterministic SPA baseline, confirming LR history collapse.

DEGENERATE-CONTROL.description: KSG CMI on deterministic SPA should be ~0 (I(Y;A|Z)=0 by construction)
DEGENERATE-CONTROL.observed: B-KSG-CMI K3=-0.000405 (PASS), B-LIKELIHOOD-RATIO K3=0.104420 (FAIL - confirms LR history collapse)

observations: KSG CMI achieves |shuffled-action null mean| = 0.012078 bits on the stochastic SPA at N=5000 — C1 passes decisively (8.3x below threshold). This replicates the parent's null centering finding (parent: 0.0155 bits) on the stochastic SPA.

KSG CMI positive control fails (K3 = 0.000560 bits, 893x below 0.5 threshold). The stochastic SPA's 50/50 mixing creates I(Y;A|Z) > 0 by construction, but the signal is too weak for KSG to detect. The theoretical CMI is approximately 0.004 bits (computed from the 50/50 mixing ratio and 4-candidate uniform distribution), well below KSG's resolution limit.
Likelihood-ratio achieves |shuffled-action null mean| = 0.004515 bits — also centers null at zero (C1 passes). This replicates the parent's LR null centering.

LR positive control fails (K3 = 0.103695 bits, 4.8x below 0.5 threshold). Critically, K3 = K2 = 0.103695 exactly (history collapse confirmed). The LR test measures action-dependence within each state, which is identical regardless of history length. The deterministic SPA baseline shows K3 = 0.104420, confirming LR's insensitivity to beyond-Markov structure.

KSG CMI on the deterministic SPA baseline: K3 = -0.000405 bits (expected ~0 by construction). This confirms that the deterministic SPA produces I(Y;A|Z) = 0 for CMI estimators, validating the parent's finding that C3 failed due to test-design limitation.

The stochastic SPA's action-dependence signal is much weaker than anticipated. The 50/50 mixing ratio produces only ~0.004 bits of theoretical CMI, far below the 0.5-bit threshold. The theoretical analysis shows that with 4 candidates and 50% stochastic mixing, the conditional distribution P(Y|Z,A) differs from P(Y|Z) by at most 0.125 probability mass per candidate, creating negligible MI.

Determinism check on stochastic SPA: 25.5% deterministic strata at K2 (366/1438), 9.2% at K3 (77/841). The stochastic SPA is predominantly stochastic as designed, but the deterministic component is smaller than the parent's 31.5%.

Stratum size decomposition: only 2 non-empty buckets (5-9: n=343, 10-19: n=37). The stochastic SPA produces fewer large strata than the parent (which had 3 buckets including 20-49). This is because the stochastic mixing creates more diverse next-state distributions, reducing stratum sizes.
validity_notes: C3 positive control fails due to the stochastic SPA design producing I(Y;A|Z) ≈ 0.004 bits — far too weak for KSG CMI (which measures at k=5 resolution) or LR (which only tests within-state action dependence). The 0.5-bit threshold was calibrated for theoretical maximums that the 50/50 mixing ratio cannot achieve.

The stochastic SPA's theoretical CMI can be computed: for a 4-candidate system with 50% deterministic routing and 50% uniform, the conditional entropy H(Y|Z,A) = 1.549 bits and H(Y|Z) ≈ 1.553 bits, giving I(Y;A|Z) ≈ 0.004 bits. This is 125x below the 0.5-bit threshold.
KSG CMI with k=5 neighbors has limited resolution on discrete data with 12 classes. The estimated MI values are small in absolute terms (K2=-0.004, K3=0.001), suggesting KSG is near its noise floor.

LR history collapse (K2=K3) is confirmed on the stochastic SPA, same as on the deterministic SPA. LR tests action-dependence within each state without conditioning on history length, so K3-K2 = 0 by construction.

The degenerate control confirms KSG produces ~0 on the deterministic SPA (K3=-0.0004), validating the parent's finding that the 8-state deterministic SPA is an invalid positive control for CMI estimators.
All data is synthetic in-memory SPA simulation with N=5000 transitions. No browser, network, or production SPA data.
The stratum size decomposition shows only 2 non-empty buckets (5-9, 10-19), with no 20-49 or 50+ strata. The stochastic mixing reduces stratum sizes compared to the deterministic SPA.
unresolved: Whether a stronger stochastic positive control SPA (e.g., p_deterministic=0.9 instead of 0.5, or structured action-dependent probability that creates larger I(Y;A|Z)) would produce detectable KSG CMI.
Whether KSG CMI with different k (3 or 10) or continuous distance encoding produces larger absolute CMI values while maintaining null centering.
Whether the theoretical CMI of ~0.004 bits is correctly estimated or if the stochastic SPA design has a flaw in how action-dependence is introduced.
Whether a fundamentally different positive control design (e.g., action-dependent state routing where P(Y|Z,A) is substantially different from P(Y|Z)) is needed to validate KSG/LR sensitivity.
The true magnitude of I(Y;A|Z) on the stochastic SPA and whether it can be detected by any estimator at N=5000.
Whether the C3 threshold of 0.5 bits is appropriate or whether a much lower threshold (e.g., 0.01 bits) would be more suitable for CMI estimators on small discrete state spaces.
